report.verdict: Emergency department management at a Level II trauma center is clear from the start, and your work backs it up with staffing, patient flow and budget results. I’d write to you about ED leadership, with your note that you’re not looking in mind.
write_up: This is a strong ED leadership profile! You show how your team changed triage and overflow beds, then give the change in patients leaving without being seen.

The Nurse Manager job is the model: it connects staffing, turnover and budget decisions to results. Your Charge Nurse job also makes your night-shift leadership and precepting work easy to understand.

Your profile isn’t what would stop me from writing. Whether a conversation makes sense also depends on the role and your interest. If you’re documenting work for a future move, the budget line is a good place to add how you planned staffing against it.

cards.where: Saguaro Valley Medical Center, Nurse Manager description
cards.line: Own a $14.5M labor budget; finished the last two fiscal years within 1% of plan.
cards.cannot_tell: The budget result is strong. For a leadership role above Nurse Manager, how you planned staffing against that budget would add to it.
